ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), within rectangle $ABCD$, a moving point $P$ starts from point $B$, travels along $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ to stop at point $A$. Let the distance traveled by point $P$ be $x$, and the area of $\triangle ABP$ be $y$. If the graph of $y$ as a function of $x$ is as shown in Figure (2), what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the analysis of the function graph, when $0<x<3$, the value of $y$ continuously increases, and $P$ moves along $BC$; when $3\le x\le 7$, the value of $y$ does not change, so $P$ moves along $CD$; when $7<x<10$, the value of $y$ continuously decreases, and $P$ moves along $DA$;\\
Hence $BC=3$, and $CD=4$\\
Because quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle\\
It follows that $AB=CD=4$\\
The area of $\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 4=\boxed{6}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure (1) shows a rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, D at the upper left, point P located on the right side BC, and line segment AP is drawn. Figure (2) is the graph of the function y with respect to x: from the origin to x=3 it is an increasing line segment; from x=3 to x=7 it is a horizontal line segment; after that it is a decreasing line segment. Reasoning: Point P starts from B, and when it first moves along BC, the base AB of △ABP is fixed, and the distance from P to AB gradually increases, so the area y gradually increases; therefore the increasing segment corresponds to BC, giving BC=3-0=3. Next, when P moves along CD, the distance from P to AB remains unchanged, so the area of △ABP remains unchanged; therefore the horizontal segment corresponds to CD, giving CD=7-3=4. In rectangle ABCD, opposite sides are equal, so AB=CD=4. △ABC is a right triangle, and its area is (1/2)×AB×BC=(1/2)×4×3=6.
